segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן מִן הַחֲלִיצָה וּמִן הַיִּיבּוּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחוֹתָהּ לֹא תִקָּח לִצְרוֹר״. בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ צָרוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ — לֹא יְהֵא לְךָ לִיקּוּחִין אֲפִילּוּ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «It is taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Shimon exempts both of them from ḥalitza and from levirate marriage, as it is stated: “And you shall not take a woman to her sister, to be a rival to her”» (Leviticus 18:18). This indicates that «at the time that» a situation arises wherein «they are to become rival wives to each other,» e.g., two sisters happen before one yavam for levirate marriage, «you shall not have» the ability «to take even one of them» in marriage. In his opinion, both women are exempt from both levirate marriage and ḥalitza at the moment that they happen before the yavam, just as a forbidden relative is exempt from both levirate marriage and ḥalitza.

moves.summary: baraita on the mishna's R' Shimon
derives exemption from 'to be a rival to her'

edges.about: from the moment the sisters stand to become rivals, neither may be taken, so both are exempt from ḥalitza and yibbum

positions.claim: both sisters are exempt from ḥalitza and yibbum
